evidence_quotes.quote: the Phiri community in Soweto have approached the court to enforce their rights of access to adequate clean water.
judges with regard to the right to access clean water, the issue of pre-paid water meters, the free basic water policy

rationale: This doctrinal legal commentary examines the South African judiciary's adjudication of the constitutional right to water in Lindiwe Mazibuko and Others v City of Johannesburg and Others (High Court, Supreme Court of Appeal and Constitutional Court) concerning the Phiri community in Soweto. Multiple legal and administrative mechanisms are co-equally central: (1) fees_tariffs_subsidies (primary), centering on the adequacy of the 6-kilolitre monthly Free Basic Water allowance, water charges above the free quota, cross-subsidization and Indigent Registration arrears write-offs and 4-kilolitre top-ups; (2) review_redress, analyzing socio-economic rights litigation to compel policy reform and the loss of billing-complaint and pre-disconnection hearing protections under prepaid meters; and (3) enforcement_sanctions, analyzing automatic halting/suspension of supply via prepaid water meters once the free allocation is exhausted (with secondary discussion of eligibility proof, registration paperwork/transport burdens and municipal outreach assistance under the Indigent Persons Policy). Outcomes are likewise multiple: effective_access (primary) focuses on water quantity/sufficiency relative to household size, continuity, reliance on unsafe surface water causing disease and women's fetching burden, alongside co-central economic_access (inability of poor households to afford prepaid water credits and receipt of free/indigent water subsidies) and administrative_outcome (automatic supply cutoffs/suspensions and judicial/policy compliance outcomes).
